name: Question 4
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/d76d928d43054c7d5c026cc25b95fb55855c7a8cbdb5fb35b5ae1f1d39a35c90.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{(y-1)^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $y,$ then over a region $D$ in the $xz$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.
worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z)$ and ${u}_{2}(x,z)$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{(y-1)^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le (y-1)^{2}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type III region. 

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/116ae6061410bca820b3c89869b23a36b5cef47e4fe483e390ee43d1e52ff726.png)

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

- The front boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
z=(y-1)^{2}\,⟹\,y=1-\sqrt{z}.
$$

- The back boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le 1-\sqrt{z}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/5613cb5b9718914e35f7259e3fe9dfd69ce128a861d19995e2c836c2b76d0f58.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $y$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{(y-1)^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{1-\sqrt{z}}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA.\end{aligned}
$$

Change the order of integration in the integral ∫02∫01∫0(y−1)2f(x,y,z)dzdydx so that it is integrated first with respect to y, then over a region D in the xz-plane. The integration region R is shown above.

a
∬D[∫11−z2f(x,y,z)dy]dA
b
∬D[∫0z2f(x,y,z)dy]dA
c
∬D[∫1zf(x,y,z)dy]dA
d
∬D[∫01−zf(x,y,z)dy]dA
e
∬D[∫z−11f(x,y,z)dy]dA
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration u1(x,z) and u2(x,z) such that

∫02∫01∫0(y−1)2f(x,y,z)dzdydx=∬D[∫u1(x,z)u2(x,z)f(x,y,z)dy]dA.

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤2,0≤y≤1,0≤z≤(y−1)2}

To change the order of integration from dzdydx to dydA, we write R as a type III region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the y-axis and in the direction of increasing y, as shown below.

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

  • The front boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x,z), is z=(y−1)2⟹y=1−z.

  • The back boundary of the region is y=0.

Therefore, the type III representation of R is

R={(x,y,z):(x,z)∈D,0≤y≤1−z},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to y and then over D, we obtain

∫02∫01∫0(y−1)2f(x,y,z)dzdydx=∬D[∫01−zf(x,y,z)dy]dA.
